recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the FHIR-30930 application in the current core build by fixing the only discovered semantic copy/paste mismatch; no further core change is recommended unless BRR separately decides to reorder or redesign ClinicalUseDefinition.library.
issue_request: FHIR-30930 was Applied/Persuasive for R5 by BRR to express complex indication logic with CQL or another Expression. It requested a top-level library canonical(Library) element and Expression-valued applicability elements under indication and contraIndication/contraindication.
initial_application: No source commit mentioning FHIR-30930 was found. Git pickaxe history found fb38294d36d8e1e37d873690a6ab931bf59d2948, titled "added CQL compatible features FHIR-30758", which added ClinicalUseDefinition.library plus the indication and contraindication applicability elements. The structural change was applied to the renamed ClinicalUseDefinition resource, but the contraindication applicability short/definition copied the indication wording.
additional_context: FHIR-30202 was the earlier nested-indication proposal and was retracted/replaced by FHIR-30930. BRR minutes from 2021-03-02 record FHIR-30930 accepted 22-0-0. source/fhir.ini lists clinicalusedefinition as the active BRR resource and ClinicalUseDefinition as normative, with the older ClinicalUseIssue name only as a commented historical entry. Zulip searches for ClinicalUseIssue/applicability/library/CQL and boolean logic indication terms found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Changed source/clinicalusedefinition/structuredefinition-ClinicalUseDefinition.xml so ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication.applicability says the expression indicates whether the contraindication is applicable. The already-correct indication applicability and top-level library element were left unchanged.
source_changes: source/clinicalusedefinition/structuredefinition-ClinicalUseDefinition.xml: changed ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication.applicability short and definition to refer to the contraindication rather than the indication.
